purpose: Investigate cancellation during assembly of actual cached solver RHS. Improve product/sum arithmetic without assuming ideal affine behavior, matched cache epochs or matched load/evaluation vectors.

reference.target: Exact real sum of supplied binary64 cached J_i times supplied binary64 load x_i, minus supplied cached residual, plus supplied limiter. No assumption of same epochs/vectors, affine law or ideal zero.
algorithm: TwoProd: p=RN(a*b); e=FMA(a,b,-p). Within guarded bounds, p+e equals exact product.

Insert each low/high product component then -residual and limiter into zero-eliminating grow expansion using general TwoSum, not FastTwoSum. Every addition replaces two terms by an exact two-term sum. Final expansion sums EXACTLY to actual cached-expression target.
Return expansion and a sequentially summed estimate with explicit conservative absolute bound gamma_n*sum(abs(expansion)), gamma_n=n*u/(1-n*u), u=2^-53. No correctly-rounded estimate claim.

domain.input_magnitudes: Each nonzero input in [2^-200,2^200], all binary64 finite; positive zero allowed. Negative zero input falls back to preserve legacy signed-zero semantics.
domain.environment: IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest ties-even, no FTZ/DAZ, no fast-math/reassociation, true fused multiply-add. Python reference assumes standard RN operations; nearest_even argument is test contract, NOT a native fenv detector. Native adapter must actually verify/set permitted environment or fallback.
domain.fallback: Outside domain/rowcap/environment => status fallback with no compensated value. Actual caller must invoke unchanged original loader, not clip values or substitute zero. Dimension mismatch is malformed input error.

proof: Every input is an integer multiple of 2^-252. Exact products therefore lie on lattice 2^-504; representable rounded products/errors and all TwoSum intermediates stay on that lattice. Any nonzero exact cancellation result is at least 2^-504, safely normal. No underflow or subnormal operation is needed in accepted domain.

Products have magnitude <=2^400; at most130 components are inserted. Input component absolute sum <2^408. A TwoSum pair has absolute sum <=(1+2u)*(abs(a)+abs(b)); fewer than17000 pair operations grow this bound by <2. Thus component/partial totals <2^409 and internal differences <2^411, far below overflow. FMA product residual is exactly representable under these normal bounds.
General TwoSum theorem then gives exact pair sums; induction over component insertions proves exact expansion target. Length <=2*n+2, no fixed truncation.

Sequential estimate has standard n-addition forward error <=gamma_n*sumabs, with no overflow/underflow by same lattice/range argument. Bound is computed as exact Fraction in reference. A native outward-rounded bound implementation would need separate review; no threshold acceptance is tied to it here.
reference.reference_fma: Python3.12 lacks math.fma in this environment. reference_fma computes exact Fraction(a)*Fraction(b)+Fraction(c), then converts once to binary64. This is a reference oracle, NOT an emitted FMA instruction or native performance/correctness validation.

illustrative_gate.residual: constructed binary64 g*(VG-GP), NOT captured native residual
illustrative_gate.interpretation: Actual cached-expression target is nonzero, unlike ideal homogeneous affine law. No promise of1e-16 accuracy/convergence or cure for full device run.

generated_code.environment: fegetround plus x86_64 MXCSR FTZ/DAZ AND rounding bits checked. Non-Linux or unsupported architecture falls back. Strict binary64 compile constants required.

native.arithmetic_contract: Reviewed exact expansion and domain proof from reference specification apply; native returns expansion plus sequential estimate. Fraction harness verifies exact actual cached-expression expansion and gamma_n sumabs estimate error. No floating error bound computed by C and no correctly-rounded estimate claim.
native.fallback_contract: Nonzero status returns count0 and NaN estimate, no compensated value. Original callback must be invoked by future adapter; this standalone kernel does not implement or approximate host fallback. Absent residual or empty contribution row falls back. Absent limiter skips validation AND insertion entirely, never synthesized as +0. Negative-zero inputs/products and zero final estimate fall back. Optional native callback semantics are not certified by this harness.
caveats: This does not fix OpenVAF or a circuit. Model/runtime/candidate unchanged; no circuit run.
